subject: Performance SLO: context window & latency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps — Performance SLOs (context window, latency)

Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to capture next steps.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: document summarization + chat for financial advisors (real-time suggestions during client calls).
- Target latency: p95 <= 250ms for short-turn replies (~0-200 tokens), p95 <= 600ms for longer context windows when streaming is enabled.
- Expected traffic: ~300 concurrent advisors during market hours; average concurrency per advisor 1.2 (mostly single active session).
- Typical context windows: 2k tokens for short sessions, up to 12k tokens for extended summaries.
- Streaming required for the advisor UI to show progressive suggestions; we’ll need to validate chunked output behavior and tail latency.

Open technical questions we agreed to validate:
1) Can we meet the p95 latency targets for 12k input+output windows with your expected concurrency and streaming?
2) Fallback behavior: if an extended-window request would violate SLOs, do you prefer degraded completeness (truncate older context) or degrade to non-streaming batch with higher latency?
3) Network egress constraints — will FinCo want a Private deployment (VPC) for lower network variance?

Next steps (owners):
- Rishi: run targeted perf benches for 2k, 8k, 12k context windows with streaming enabled; provide rough token/sec and p95 numbers by EOD 4/12.
- Neha: prepare SLO proposal (SLA language + fallback policies) and attach a recommended configuration (batching, kv-cache, quantization profile) — draft by 4/12.
- Marissa: coordinate follow-up meeting with FinCo engineering to review benchmarks and pick rollout plan — propose times 4/13-4/15.

Attachments: I’m attaching our Q1 latency benchmark summary and a draft SLO proposal for FinCo to review.

If any detail is incorrect, call it out and I’ll update.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

---
Attachment: redwood_latency_benchmarks_q1.pdf (summary of lab runs; synthetic load, various model sizes)
Attachment: slo_proposal_finco_v1.pdf (initial SLO wording and fallback options)

From: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinCo Platform <platform@finco.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Performance SLOs (context window, latency)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The 250ms p95 is a hard goal for short replies (advisors expect near-interactive feel). If you can show p95 < 200ms in your bench for the 0-200 token path that’d be great.
- For extended sessions (8–12k tokens), we’re willing to accept up to 700ms p95 as long as streaming delivers incremental tokens to the client (so the advisor sees progress).
- Fallback preference: prefer truncation of older context (keep the most recent tokens) over switching to non-streaming mode. We want progressive UX.

Also: we are bound by strict egress logging and audit policies — likely we’ll look at a VPC/private deployment. I looped in platform@finco.com for the rest of the infra questions.

Can Rishi/Neha confirm the test plan and share expected metrics?

—Tom

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Performance SLOs (context window, latency)

Tom/Marissa — thanks. Quick note on bench approach so expectations are clear: 
- We’ll run end-to-end benches from the Redwood hosted region closest to FinCo (us-west-2) with a Private VPC-equivalent network overlay to mimic egress constraints.
- Models: we’ll test a medium-sized open LLM (7–13B) and a quantized 70B variant to show tradeoffs.
- Scenarios: 0–200 tokens (interactive), 2k tokens, 8k tokens, 12k tokens. Each scenario will be run at 1x, 3x, and 5x of your reported concurrent load to surface degradation points.
- Metrics reported: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail jitter, throughput (tokens/sec), and streaming chunk size vs chunk latency.

Preliminary expectation: for a 7–13B model with optimized kernels and KV caching, interactive path p95 should be < 200ms at 300 concurrent users. For 12k windows streaming, p95 can approach 500–700ms depending on IO and chunking strategy — will confirm with numbers.

Deliverable: a bench report (CSV + short writeup) and config suggestions by COB 4/12.

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: SLO proposal (draft) — streaming, truncation, concurrency

Tom — draft SLO attached and a short summary inline: 
- Interactive path (0–200 tokens): p95 <= 200ms, availability 99.9% (excl. scheduled maint).
- Large context (8k–12k tokens) streaming: p95 <= 700ms, progressive chunk delivery with max chunk latency 150ms.
- Concurrency target: support 300 concurrent advisor sessions with graceful degradation to 200 concurrent sessions under sustained load via vertical autoscaling/burst policy.
- Fallback policy: automatic context truncation (drop oldest 20% of tokens when request would exceed configured latency profile) before switching to non-streaming mode.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and audit log forwarding to FinCo SIEM.

I attached the SLO PDF and a short recommended runtime configuration: batching window 8–12ms, KV cache enabled for repeated contexts, and suggestions on quantization that reduce memory while keeping latency predictable.

If this matches your expectations I’ll turn it into an SLA paragraph and legal-ready wording.

-Neha
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: slo_proposal_finco_v1.pdf

From: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO proposal (draft) — streaming, truncation, concurrency

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. A few quick asks before we lock the SLA language: 
1) Can you add a short section that explains the UX impact of truncating older context (examples: 2–3 sentence summaries that advise the advisor when older context has been dropped)?
2) For the private/VPC deployment, what additional latency variance should we expect compared to hosted (ballpark)? A +/- 30–50ms network variance is fine, but we need to plan for it.

If you can include those two items in the next iteration we can move to legal review and lock in a pilot start date of 5/3.

Appreciate the quick turnaround team — let’s sync after the bench runs and we’ll pick a pilot configuration.

—Tom
